text:
Jules T.: Hi all, I'm on my first on-call rotation starting Monday. Short list of things I need sorted: VPN/runbook access, a buddy to shadow for the first 24h shift, and any quick practice drills I can run locally. Also, who signs off that I'm ready to take solo shifts?

Maya R. (oncall-lead): Welcome Jules! :tada: Buddy system is standard: we pair new folks for the first 2 shifts. I can assign one now. Sign-off is done by the oncall lead after two successful shadowed shifts + one simulated drill.

Infra Bot: Account update: Jules T. added to PagerDuty (standard-oncall), email invite sent. Runbook group read access granted for /runbooks/oncall at 2024-11-10T15:12Z.

Priya S.: I can be your buddy for Monday's shift (04:00-12:00 UTC). I'll walk you through the triage checklist and how we open an incident channel. Also I'll send the tabletop scenario we use for training.

Jules T.: Thanks Priya, that time works. Quick question: can I practice without generating real alerts? I don't want to disturb production.

DevEx: We have a sandbox alerting namespace and a CLI simulator. Try `rw-sim alert create --severity P0 --service inference --scenario latency-spike`. It will create a fake incident and simulate the PD flow and channel creation. Docs: https://redwood.internal/devex/oncall-sim

Maya R. (oncall-lead): Good — use the sim. Also do the mini-drill in #incidents-sim this Friday at 16:00 PT. It's a 30-min tabletop: someone plays SRE, someone plays infra, we go through runbook steps and postmortem template.

Jules T.: Where's the runbook canonical path? I want to skim the failover and cache-eviction sections.

Priya S.: Runbooks are on the wiki: https://wiki.internal/redwood/runbooks/oncall. The failover play is at /runbooks/oncall/runtime-failover.md and cache eviction is /runbooks/oncall/cache-issues.md. Both require SSO (okta) or office VPN. If VPN issues, ping #help and tag "vpn-access".

Maya R. (oncall-lead): Two quick operational notes: 1) If you get a page, ack within 2 minutes. If you can't reach the box in 5 minutes, escalate. 2) For P0 we always open an incident channel named incident-<PDID>-<short>, e.g., incident-PD1234-runtime. Include initial impact, owner, and live links to metrics.

Jules T.: Ack window noted. For tools, what are the first commands I should run to triage runtime issues?

Priya S.: Triage starter pack (keep handy):
```
ssh redwood@ops-box
kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | grep redwood-runtime
kubectl logs -n inference <pod> -c runtime --since=5m | tail -n 200
curl -fS http://health.internal/ready || echo "health check failed"
```
Also check the APM dashboard link in the runbook for latency traces.

DevEx: Also run `rw incident checklist start` on the devbox for an interactive walk-through. It will guide new ons for playbook steps and create a mock channel if used with --dry-run.

Priya S.: One more thing: post-incident writeups use the team template. Required fields: summary, severity, timeline, actions taken, root cause, mitigation, and assigned follow-ups with clear owners and due dates. Keep it under 900 words if possible. Maya will review the first one.

Jules T.: Thanks everyone. I'll join Friday's sim and try the CLI sim tonight. See you on Monday with Priya as my buddy. :smiley:
